Emily — quick sizing notes (cc Marissa/Vivek):

- Suggested baseline pool: 4 x A10G (inference-optimized) + 2 x A100-light for peak burst for model types with larger KV caches. That maps roughly to your 6 K80-equivalent target while keeping headroom.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~360–420 tokens/sec depending on sequence length distribution and batching. We can guarantee a 350 t/s 99th-percentile SLO for the committed pool if you take a 24m or 36m term and enable our autoscaling cushion + prefix caching.
- Burst handling: allow a burst buffer (capacity tier) that covers up to 700 t/s for short windows (up to 30 seconds/occurrence) with automatic graceful degradation if sustained. We can also define a priority routing policy so critical traffic always has reserved capacity.

Ramp proposal (example):
- Month 0 (contract signed): provisioning and baseline config; dry-run & preflight (no traffic)
- Month 1: +30% of committed capacity (staged nodes online, warm caches)
- Month 2–3: ramp to 60% then 100% committed capacity
- Month 4: enable sustained burst ops and finalize performance tuning

If you prefer an earlier start date for critical workloads we can shift the ramp and add temporary burst credits for the first quarter.

I'll include a short SRE playbook excerpt in the SOW draft.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Carlos/Emily — quick answers from commercial/legal side (looping Laura for the SOW/TS&A redlines):

1) Billing cadence: we can support quarterly billing against an annual committed value for 24 and 36 month contracts. For 12 month terms we typically require monthly or upfront payment, but we can be flexible with credit approvals.
2) Price escalators: discounts are guaranteed for the term of the contract — list prices may change, but your contracted unit price is fixed for the committed term. We do allow an index-linked adjustment if customers specifically request it, but that's rare for standard enterprise arrangements.
3) Start-date credits: if Redwood misses the mutually agreed start date by >14 calendar days we will provide a pro-rated credit equal to the committed monthly fee for each week of delay beyond the 14-day grace period, up to one full month, OR optionally grant equivalent burst credits (your choice). We'll write the precise calculation into the SOW.
4) Early termination: for 24m we can offer a stepped exit schedule: 50% of remaining committed value in year 1, 35% in year 2 (negotiable based on final discount and commit size). For 36m the exit fee is lower (reflects longer term pricing).

Laura — can you prepare a redlineable SOW that includes the ramp timeline, start-date credit formula, and the exit schedule?

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
